title: Dixieland, rock and roll and boogie woogie today
summary: They discuss the style the current band plays, requests for old tunes at holiday dances, boogie woogie versus rock and roll, and why Dixieland lasts.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Now there's some people here in New Iberia, they are high and they want Dixon. Uh huh. That's when you play anything else, they want to ask you to stop. What style does Mr. Wilson's band, what style do you play in? Well we try to satisfy the people, try to give them some of the present day stuff.
I say that the main style is Dixon-led.
That's why I said we try.
As well as that rock and roll is some kind of knowledge in it.
Do you still play some of the old arrangements or did you work out in years past? Do you try to get some of the ideas in them that you've had in the past? A few. Uh huh.

Especially around the holiday dances around New Year's and Christmas time. That's when they really go into it. The saints go marching in and tiger rank and all stuff like that. I don't think people ever get tired of those tutus.
Do they ask you to play any boogie woogie in any of these pieces here or places that you do you play for them?
Yes we do. And it's mostly among the younger people.
When you find the older set, I mean you don't have that boogie woogie without at all. Is boogie woogie on its way out now do you think or is it still pretty strong?
Rock and roll is kind of smothering it right now if you ask me.
Well I don't think that would be anything that would die out.

I think rock and roll is somewhat on the same footing as this bebop that they had it. It was out in a blast for a while and all of a sudden it just died out. That rock and roll I don't think it'll last too long either. It might but I doubt it.

I noticed some of the numbers on the jukebox now they're kind of getting away from rock and roll some of the numbers. Some people seem to think that rock and roll is less but I don't. It's kind of hard to say. Why would you say that the Dixieland style seems to be the most lasting of all? Is there any special reason that you would have been on? I think I think and there was more music. A musician at that time had to learn to execute his instrument more than the, the, with this rock and roll. Yeah there's not anything very complex about that. And then the Dixieland when they were playing everybody, everybody was awake. Who was better than them? It was competition between the boys. Exactly. That's right. Well that was the style of music I guess we used. That's right. We have to play. That's right. They have us enough to.
